title: Tent City funding and housing revitalization delays
subtitle: Committee backs steady funding for A Better Tent City and asks for options to advance Mooregate redevelopment.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended keeping annual funding for A Better Tent City at $236,390 and sending that decision to the 2026 budget process {{vote:m1}}. A delegate from the organization had asked for $180,000 more for dedicated safety and housing staff. The committee did not recommend that increase, and staff will gather more information on the security concerns.

The committee also considered a staff report that proposes delaying the Mooregate redevelopment by one year and pushing the Courtland-Shelley and 140 Weber Street projects beyond 2030, because of debt costs. It recommended that staff report back by the end of Q1 2026 on funding and financing options to build Mooregate within one year, and on partnership opportunities {{vote:m2}}.

This matters to residents because the regional housing waitlist has passed 11,000 applications and is growing. These are recommendations only. Council will decide during the 2026 budget process, and the committee also received a seasonal illness report for information.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region consider maintaining annual funding of $236,390 for A Better Tent City and refer the decision to the 2026 budget process.

The committee recommended that staff report by the end of Q1 2026 on funding and financing options to advance Mooregate construction within one year, and update the earlier report on affordable housing partnerships and site readiness.

debate: A delegate from A Better Tent City asked for $180,000 more per year for dedicated safety and housing staff. The delegate said residents are ready to move on but there are too few affordable places, and that the site needs someone to coordinate safety before visitors return.

One councillor supported keeping the current funding because it fits within the budget target of under 5% and said an increase would open the door to more requests. Others valued the stability of including it in the budget. One councillor asked for more information on the security issues, and staff said they would ask the organization to provide it.

Staff said the Mooregate delay is meant to smooth out debt costs, but a one-year delay does not solve debt servicing on its own. Staff warned that close to $75 million in federal funding for the project is at risk, and that the new Build Canada Homes program is still unclear.

Supporters of the Mooregate motion said it makes no budget decision and keeps all options open, including partnerships with non-profits and the private sector and getting the site ready in the meantime. Staff said the project is shovel ready.

One councillor opposed the motion, calling cuts to housing and community services a false economy and noting the long waitlist. The mover and another councillor replied that the motion only asks for information and contains no cutback.
